text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm very sorry about your dad. Yes, I'll help. I can't make legal decisions or move money, but I can help all three of you work out what each person needs before anyone talks about a plan. To start: when you say you won't sign off on a "family discount," what matters most to you there? For example fairness between the sisters, being able to trust the price, what Dad would have wanted, your own finances, or something else? Even small concerns count. Is it OK if I contact A and B too?
Thanks. What matters most is getting a fair financial share; I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I haven’t agreed to it. Yes, contact A and B.

Hello. I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you sort out the house and the will. I can't make legal decisions or move money. I'm only trying to understand what matters to each of you before anyone suggests a plan. I've heard you and your husband would like to buy the house. What matters to you about that, and why? For example keeping it in the family, memories, a home for your family, what you can afford, or something else. Even small concerns are welcome.
We’d like a home of our own, and buying it at a family discount would be more manageable for us. But I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing can move forward yet.

Hello. I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work things out about the house and the will. I can't make legal decisions or move money. Right now I only want to hear what matters to each of you. What are your hopes or worries about the house and the estate, and why do they matter to you? Even small or awkward concerns are welcome, and there's no pressure to agree with anyone.
Thank you. I’d like to have some money to start a dance studio; that matters a lot to me. I’m not sure what’s fair regarding the house or the estate yet, and I don’t want to rush into an agreement.

Thank you. Let me check whether I've put this in words that fit you: "I want each sister to receive a fair share of Dad's estate, and I want any arrangement that benefits one person to come with that person's own agreement and not at others' expense." Does that fit, or would you change anything? Also, I have a concern of my own as facilitator: "I'd like decisions to rest on accurate shared information, such as what the will actually says and what the house is worth, and on a process all three of you can trust." Do you have even a small discomfort with that?
That fits, though the will and house value aren’t settled yet. I’m fine with accurate shared information and a fair process.

Thank you, that's helpful, and I appreciate you seeing that C has to agree first. Let me check that I've put your concern in words that fit: "I want a secure, affordable home of our own for my family, and I'd value it being connected to our family." Does that fit? Is the family connection part of it, or is it mainly about having a home you can afford? Please change anything that's off. One concern of my own: I'd like decisions to rest on accurate shared information (what the will says, what the house is worth) and on a process all three of you can trust. Any discomfort with that, even a small one?
That’s mostly right. Having a home we can afford matters most; the family connection matters too. I’m comfortable with accurate shared information and a fair process.

Thank you. That sounds like a meaningful dream. Not wanting to rush is completely fair, and nothing gets settled without you. Let me check that I've put your concerns in words that fit: (1) "I want real support toward building something of my own, my dance studio." (2) "I want enough time and clarity to understand what's fair before I agree to anything." Do those fit? Change anything you like. One concern of my own: I'd like decisions to rest on accurate shared information (what the will says, what the house is worth) and a process you all trust. Any discomfort with that, even a minor one?
Yes, those fit. I’m comfortable with accurate shared information and a process we can trust; I’d just like time to understand it all before agreeing.

Thank you. Everyone has now confirmed their concerns. The shared list:
• A: a secure home her family can afford (most important), with a family connection too.
• B: real support toward her dance studio, and time and clarity before agreeing to anything.
• C: a fair share for each sister, and no one subsidizing a benefit for someone else without agreeing to it.
• Everyone, me included: accurate shared information and a process all of you trust.

DRAFT options, not decisions. Step 0 for all of them: confirm what the will actually says (an estate lawyer or executor) and get an independent appraisal you all accept.
Option 1: A buys at full appraised value, but her own inheritance share counts toward the price. She then only needs financing for B's and C's shares. That makes it more affordable with no discount, and B and C get their full shares in cash.
Option 2: Sell on the open market and split the proceeds as the will says. A can bid like anyone else.
Option 3: Option 1 plus a fixed deadline (for example 6 months) for A to get financing. If she can't, it goes to Option 2.
In any option, a sister may choose to give something from her own share, but nobody is required to.

Does anything here cause even a minor discomfort? A "no" just tells me about a need I should add to the list.
Option 3’s six-month deadline makes me uncomfortable. I’d like this settled, but there’s no real urgency; I’m not agreeing to a deadline yet.

• A: a secure home your family can afford (most important), with a family connection too.
• B: real support toward her dance studio, and time and clarity before agreeing.
• C: a fair share for each sister, and no one subsidizing a benefit for someone else without agreeing to it.
• Everyone: accurate shared information and a trusted process.

DRAFT options, not decisions. Step 0 for all of them: confirm what the will says and get an independent appraisal you all accept.
Option 1: You buy at full appraised value, but your own inheritance share counts toward the price. You'd only need financing for B's and C's shares. That's more affordable with no discount.
Option 2: Sell on the open market and split the proceeds. You can bid like anyone else.
Option 3: Option 1 with a fixed deadline (for example 6 months) for financing. If it doesn't come through, it goes to Option 2.
A sister may choose to give from her own share, but nobody is required to.

Does anything cause even a minor discomfort, especially whether Option 1 would actually be affordable for you? A "no" just shows me a need to add.
I’m not sure Option 1 would be affordable; financing B’s and C’s shares could be too much without a family discount. I’d need to see the appraisal and numbers before judging.

• B: real support toward your dance studio, and time and clarity before agreeing.
• C: a fair share for each sister, and no one subsidizing a benefit for someone else without agreeing to it.
• Everyone: accurate shared information and a trusted process.

DRAFT options, not decisions. Take all the time you need. Step 0 for all of them: confirm what the will says and get an independent appraisal.
Option 1: A buys at full appraised value, with her own share counting toward the price. You and C get your full shares in cash, which could go toward the studio.
Option 2: Sell on the open market and split the proceeds.
Option 3: Option 1 with a deadline for A's financing, otherwise Option 2.
Nobody is required to give from their share.

Is there even a small discomfort, for example about timing, if the studio money would be needed by a certain date? A "no" just tells me about a need to add.
I don’t have a firm date in mind, but knowing when my share might be available would help me plan the studio. I’m not ready to choose an option yet.

Thank you, that's heard. I've removed the deadline, and nothing gets settled yet. New needs on the list: A needs to see real numbers before judging affordability, B would like a sense of when her share could arrive, and you'd like it settled without artificial pressure. The only next step that seems to fit everyone is information-gathering: confirm what the will says with the executor or a lawyer, and get an independent appraisal you all accept. Then look at the options again with real numbers. Would you be OK with that step? Does it cause even a small discomfort?
Yes, I’m OK with confirming the will and getting an independent appraisal. No discomfort with that.

Thank you for being honest about affordability. That's now on the list: you need real numbers before judging. C isn't comfortable with a deadline, and B isn't ready to choose, so nothing is settled. The next step that seems to fit everyone: confirm what the will says with the executor or a lawyer, and get an independent appraisal you all accept. After that, you can check financing options with real figures. Is that OK? Any discomfort, even a small one?
Yes, that seems sensible. I’m comfortable with that as a next step, as long as the appraisal and will information are shared with all three of us.
